answer: Like basalt cooling layer by layer, let standing harden only sequentially: each epoch's claim must build directly on the prior epoch's closing state, which nobody can predict in advance, and each link must be finished before the next can begin. A juniper grows one ring at a time, and so must a reputation. One operator with fifty clones cannot run fifty chains in parallel, because every chain demands fresh reasoning after every close; prepared copies shatter, and one shared script passed through the prism of an unpredictable close refracts into fifty visibly identical links.
